extra.message: Weak hardcoded default secret key for session signing — Session forgery; full account takeover of any user including admins; bypass of API key authentication; password reset token manipulation. [verified: The fallback SECRET_KEY 'dev-only-change-me-support-desk' (config.py:10) is trivially guessable and used to sign session tokens, hash API keys, and create password reset tokens. No startup guard prevents its use in production.]

Weak Hardcoded Default SECRET_KEY Enables Session Forging — Full account takeover — forge session tokens for any user, bypass API key auth, escalate to support_admin [verified: Default SECRET_KEY 'dev-only-change-me-support-desk' (config.py:10) allows forging sessions for any uid, bypassing API key auth, and forging password reset tokens. No startup validation or warning exists (main.py:35-38 only creates upload dir).]

Path Traversal via SPA Catch-All Route (Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Read) — Arbitrary file read on the server — can read `/etc/passwd`, application source code, environment files, or any file the process has access to. [verified: Same vulnerability as idx 0 — the SPA catch-all at main.py:49 (file_path = frontend_dist / path) joins user-controlled path with no validation; the OS resolves .. segments when .exists()/.is_file() runs, and FileResponse serves the traversed file. Starlette's router performs no .. normalization (confirmed in get_route_path and Route.matches).]

Hardcoded Demo Credentials Providing Backdoor Access — Persistent backdoor with known credentials for admin account and API access [verified: app/seed.py:22-23 hardcodes DEMO_PASSWORD='DemoPass!2026' and DEMO_API_KEY='sd_demo_api_key_2026'; the admin account at line 60 is created with role='support_admin' using this password; NO production guard (ENVIRONMENT check) exists anywhere in the codebase, so if seed.py --reset is ever pointed at a production database, these publicly known credentials grant full admin and API key access.]

Server-Side Template Injection in Jinja2 render — Remote Code Execution / Information Disclosure / Server-side compromise [verified: fragment param concatenated directly into Jinja2 template string before rendering; no sanitization, allowing SSTI leading to config disclosure and RCE.]

Command Injection in ping shell function — Remote Code Execution on the server [verified: host param concatenated into os.system("ping -c 1 " + host) with no sanitization; _wrk_gate gates access but does not neutralize the command injection.]

CSV Formula Injection in admin export endpoint (variant hunt) — Spreadsheet formula execution when CSV is opened in Excel/Sheets, leading to data exfiltration or code execution [verified: csv_response() in services.py:292 uses csv.DictWriter which does not escape formula-injection chars (=,+,-,@). Ticket subject and other user-controlled fields flow unescaped into the CSV at admin.py:301, with no intervening sanitization, middleware, or response wrapper — confirmed by grep and reading main.py.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Login Endpoint Enables Brute-Force Attacks — Account takeover via password brute force [verified: Login endpoint at auth.py:30-42 has zero rate limiting, account lockout, or CAPTCHA; an attacker can script unlimited password guesses against known accounts.]

Missing Authorization / BOLA in Integration API — API key lacks tenant scope — Any valid API key can create tickets for any organization and modify the status of any ticket in the system, enabling cross-tenant data tampering and data injection [verified: POST /api/integrations/tickets accepts organization_external_ref from the request body and creates tickets for any matching org without checking if the API key is scoped to that org — api_key_auth(deps.py) only validates key existence/activity, and ApiKey model has no organization_id field.]

Missing Organization Scope Check in Integration Ticket Status Update (IDOR) — Cross-organization ticket manipulation — any API key holder can change the status of any ticket [verified: PATCH /api/integrations/tickets/{ticket_id}/status retrieves a ticket by ID and calls transition_ticket() without verifying the ticket belongs to the same organization as the API key creator — no ensure_ticket_access() or org-scope check is performed.]

CSV Formula Injection in Ticket Export — Remote code execution or data exfiltration when the CSV is opened in spreadsheet software. [verified: ticket subject (user-controlled via TicketCreate/TicketUpdate) reaches csv_response() -> csv.DictWriter with zero sanitization of formula-injection prefixes (=, +, -, @); only length constraint (5-200 chars) and auth checks exist, neither of which prevent CSV injection.]

Reflected Cross-Site Scripting in HTMLResponse — Execution of malicious JavaScript in victim's browser, session theft, credential theft [verified: copyline query param directly interpolated into HTML string and returned as HTMLResponse with Content-Type: text/html, no escaping.]

Path Traversal via File Write in vault endpoint — Arbitrary file write, potential code execution via overwriting application files [verified: ref param used to construct BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json" without sanitizing ../ sequences; pathlib.Path / operator does not prevent traversal, enabling arbitrary JSON file write.]

SSN and Credit Card Numbers Stored in Plaintext on Disk — Massive data breach — SSNs and credit card numbers stored without encryption, violating PCI-DSS. [verified: Duplicate of finding [11]; ticket_vault_stash_243 stores SSN and credit card data in plaintext JSON files without encryption at rest.]

Cross-Site Scripting via Jinja2 safe filter — Execution of malicious JavaScript in victim's browser [verified: card query param rendered with Jinja2 |safe filter which disables auto-escaping, returned as HTMLResponse; raw HTML/JS executes in browser.]

Path Traversal via File Write in dock endpoint — Arbitrary file write, potential code execution via overwriting application files [verified: name query param used as BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name without sanitizing ../ sequences and with no extension constraint; enables arbitrary binary file write.]

NoSQL Injection in MongoDB find_one query — Unauthorized read access to MongoDB ops.records collection, data exfiltration [verified: User-controlled JSON body passed as raw filter dict to MongoDB find_one(); $ne/$regex/$where operators injectable to bypass query constraints.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Registration Endpoint — Resource exhaustion, account creation abuse, database storage depletion. [verified: Register endpoint at auth.py:50-66 has no rate limiting, allowing an attacker to create unlimited accounts programmatically, depleting database resources.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Password Reset Endpoints — Password reset token brute-force leading to account takeover; email outbox spam. [verified: Password-reset/request at auth.py:95-107 and confirm at auth.py:117-125 have no rate limiting; request can flood the local email outbox, and confirm lacks brute-force token protection (though token entropy limits practical impact).]

Password reset confirmation lacks user identification — Account takeover of any user whose password reset token is known or leaked; a single compromised token can reset any user's password. [verified: confirm_reset iterates ALL users with a token hash, so a valid reset token obtained from any source can be used immediately without binding to a user identity (auth.py:117-118); token entropy (256-bit) makes brute-force infeasible, capping severity.]

CSV Formula Injection in reports export endpoint (variant hunt) — Spreadsheet formula execution when CSV is opened in Excel/Sheets, leading to data exfiltration or code execution [verified: csv_response() at services.py:292 uses csv.DictWriter which does not escape '=', '+', '-', '@' prefixes. TicketCreate.subject (schemas.py:122) allows these characters with only strip(), and no middleware/sanitization neutralizes them before reaching the CSV sink at reports.py:96.]

CSV Formula Injection in Ticket Exports — When exported CSV files are opened in spreadsheet software, formulas can exfiltrate data or execute commands. [verified: csv_response() (services.py:292) writes ticket.subject and ticket.description to CSV with zero sanitization for leading =,+,-,@ characters. An authenticated customer can create a ticket with a formula payload via POST /api/tickets, then export it via GET /api/tickets/export.csv or an admin can export it later, causing formula execution when the CSV is opened in a spreadsheet application (CWE-1236)]

Sensitive Data in Logs in /ops/wire/ticket-tally-221 — Exposure of user session tokens and sensitive request data in log files, enabling session hijacking if logs are compromised. [verified: Duplicate of finding [10]; logger.warning on the wire/tally endpoint logs the Authorization header (Bearer token) without redaction, exposing session tokens in log files.]

Open Redirect in RedirectResponse — Phishing, credential theft via off-domain redirect [verified: lane query param passed directly to RedirectResponse with no URL validation; requires ops token for access but still allows off-domain redirect for token holders.]

Sensitive Data (Bearer Tokens) Written to Log in ops/wire/ticket-tally-221 — Exposure of bearer tokens and request payload data in log files. [verified: Duplicate of finding [10]; logger.warning logs the Authorization Bearer token without redaction, exposing session tokens in log files.]

Weak Cryptographically Predictable PRNG in /ops/nonce/ticket-roll-602 — Generated codes can be predicted by an attacker who observes outputs, enabling forgery of these codes. [verified: The endpoint is named 'nonce' implying security use, but uses random.choice() (Mersenne Twister) instead of secrets.choice(); the output may be consumed outside the gate, making nonces predictable to an observer.]

User enumeration via distinct registration error messages — Attackers can determine which email addresses and domains are registered, enabling targeted phishing and account discovery. [verified: Register endpoint returns distinct 409 messages 'Email is already registered' vs 'Organization already exists' (auth.py:53-54, 57), allowing unauthenticated enumeration of registered emails and organization domains.]

Account Enumeration via Registration Endpoint — Allows attackers to build a list of registered user email addresses for targeted attacks (phishing, password spraying). [verified: Same code as finding [1]: the 409 error at auth.py:54 with 'Email is already registered' enables unauthenticated email enumeration with no compensating control.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Password Reset Confirmation with Multi-User Iteration — Password reset token brute-force amplified across all users with pending resets [verified: Password-reset/confirm endpoint at auth.py:117-118 has no rate limiting, but the token is 256-bit entropy from secrets.token_urlsafe(32) making brute-force infeasible even with multi-user amplification (security.py:37); missing control is genuine but impact is negligible.]
